boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Chalk Bluff record (May 1-2, 1863) in Marmaduke's Second Expedition into Missouri [April-May 1863]. The rear-guard fighting from Jackson to Bloomfield (April 27-30) is context; the May 1 fighting on the road to Chalk Bluff and the May 2 crossing fall within the frozen interval and are one record. Campaign-wide marches, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 2nd Division, Army of the Frontier and force under command of Brig. Gen. John McNeil [US] and Marmaduke's Cavalry Division [CS], with no numerical bounds; the live field reads zero. Vandever wrote on April 30 that all accounts put the enemy at 7,000 or 8,000 with ten guns. Marmaduke says his effective fighting force did not exceed 3,500 and the enemy had about 8,000 with fifteen guns; Vandever says he played ten guns on the enemy at Chalk Bluff.
claims.rationale: Interested estimates of the other side and an effective-force figure for the retreat. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Marmaduke says the Saint Francis was much swollen, rapid, unbridged and without ferry-boats, and that he formed a dismounted line about four miles from the crossing. Vandever says he shelled the enemy before they could get out of the bottom on the far side, and that the pursuit ran over bad roads and destroyed bridges.

Marmaduke says he expected no trouble except in crossing the Saint Francis.
claims.rationale: Attributed knowledge from interested dispatches and a report; no original orders inspected.

Vandever says he meant to follow and punish the enemy and drive him from the State, and that after the crossing he was ordered back to Bloomfield.

claims.value: Vandever says he assigned McNeil the advance throughout the pursuit because of his knowledge of the country, and that he was himself shelling the enemy across the river on May 2. Marmaduke says he dismounted most of his command to hold the line while the rest crossed. NPS says Vandever pursued and Marmaduke formed a rear guard. The frozen commanders are Brigadier Generals William Vandever and John S. Marmaduke; the live page lists both without ranks.
claims.rationale: Command roles from interested reports and a summary; the listed commanders do not receive automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Confederate tactical victory, adding that the results forced Marmaduke to end his expedition, making it a Union strategic victory; the live result reads Confederate Victory (tactical). Marmaduke says his whole command was safely across by sunup and the pursuit ceased. Vandever says he drove the enemy across with heavy loss, though he saved his guns.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The strategic gloss in the frozen text is campaign contribution, not tactical outcome.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Unknown; the live field reads zero. Vandever wrote on May 2 that his whole loss would not exceed 50, that Lieutenant Eaton was killed by the premature explosion of a Union shell, that many enemy dead and wounded lay along the road, and on May 4 that 19 enemy dead lay together after one charge. NPS says the raiders suffered heavy casualties. Marmaduke's expedition total is recorded under Cape Girardeau and not assigned here.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Vandever's 50 may cover the whole pursuit; the live zero is not measured absence.

open_questions: McNeil's May 12 report on the pursuit (read and not selected; a fourth family for this record), Caldwell's and La Grange's reports (Nos. 5, 7), the Union addenda return (No. 1), the Confederate brigade reports (Nos. 14-19) and any map of the crossing remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. McNeil's April 26, 1863 dispatches from Cape Girardeau and Vandever's April 30-May 4 dispatches are separate author families of interested Union accounts; Marmaduke's May 20, 1863 report is one family of interested Confederate accounts, and Kirby Smith's printed indorsement and the compiled addenda return (garbled in OCR) are not counted as further families. Official Records Series I, Volume XXII, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
